title: SpaceX Launches Classified USSF-259 Mission from Vandenberg, Lands 662nd Booster
detail: SpaceX launched the classified USSF-259 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:07 p.m. PDT on Sept 16, 2026 (01:07 UTC Sept 17) — a day after standing down from the original Sept 15 attempt prior to fueling, with no reason disclosed. The Falcon 9 first stage, B1097, flew for a record 13th time; it previously launched Sentinel-6B, Twilight, NROL-172, Transporter-17 and eight Starlink missions. About 8.5 minutes after liftoff, B1097 landed on the 'Of Course I Still Love You' droneship in the Pacific — SpaceX's 662nd booster landing, its 108th Falcon-family launch of 2026, and its third national-security Vandenberg launch in a month.

title: Starship Flight 14 Slips Again, Now Targeting September 28
detail: SpaceX announced Sept 17, 2026 that Starship Flight 14 — the program's first attempt at reaching full orbital velocity and deploying operational Starlink V3 satellites — has slipped again, from the previously targeted Sept 22 to no earlier than Sept 28, pending regulatory approval. The company gave no explanation for the latest six-day delay, the third schedule change in as many weeks. The 75-minute launch window remains set to open at 7:15 a.m. CT (8:15 a.m. EDT) from Starbase, Texas. Booster 21 and Ship 41 have completed their static-fire campaigns (B21's 33-engine test Aug 28; Ship 41's six-engine test Aug 21) and remain in final Starbase checkout ahead of stacking.
